html:
The Nasa, long called the Páez, are an Indigenous people of the Andes of Cauca in southwestern Colombia, especially the region of Tierradentro, whose valleys also hold the painted underground tombs of an older culture. Their language, Nasa Yuwe, has no proven relatives.

From the 1500s the Nasa resisted the Spanish fiercely from their steep valleys. Legend remembers La Gaitana, a woman chief who led a rising after a Spanish captain burned her son alive. In colonial times they won resguardos, communal reserves under their own chiefs. In the 1910s Manuel Quintín Lame, a Nasa, led a movement to recover stolen land, and in 1971 the Nasa helped found the Regional Indigenous Council of Cauca, a model for Indigenous organising across the country. Their unarmed Indigenous Guard has faced violence from guerrillas, paramilitaries and the army. Their neighbours include the Misak (Guambiano).
